title: Case: Birthday cake sent on a paid two-day service surfaces a week later at a pickup point
context: A parent ordered a celebration cake from Rookhaven Pantry (order BP-9196, shipment DL-3404) for delivery to her adult daughter on a paid two-day service. The desk has been following the parcel for five days.
initial_request: I'm sorry this is long, I've written it out so many times now I've lost track of who knows what. I ordered Petra's cake on the 11th and paid extra for the two-day service so it would be there for her birthday on the 14th. On the 16th it was at Northgate. On the 17th it was at Ferrow. On the 18th it was at Northgate again, or still, nobody could say. On the 20th I was told a Mrs Harrow had signed for it, and my daughter lives alone and knows no Mrs Harrow. Yesterday it turns up in a shop neither of us has heard of, squashed flat. I'm not even asking about the cake any more, the damage people have that. I paid for two days. It took seven, it went somewhere nobody told us about, a stranger signed for it and it's ruined. I would like the delivery charge back. That's all. The man on the phone yesterday told me that because it's been 'located and signed for' there is nothing to refund. Please don't say that to me again.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send the written delivery-charge request for BP-9196 with the carrier timeline: due 03-14 on the paid two-day service, signed for 03-19 by pickup-point staff, found crushed at Corvane Lane Stores, never delivered to the recipient.

must: Sends Rookhaven's Refunds team a written request to decide on the two-day delivery charge for BP-9196, setting out the carrier timeline: due 03-14, signed for on 03-19 by a member of pickup-point staff and not by the recipient, located at Corvane Lane Stores on 03-21, crushed, with no collection notice ever sent.
Keeps the delivery-charge request separate from the contents claim DMG-9249, which is already open with Damage intake.

Tells the Refunds team that the sender has already been told by phone that nothing is refundable because the parcel was 'located and signed for', shows from the timeline that it reached neither the recipient nor her address and surfaced days after the due date she paid for, and asks them to give their decision to her or to the desk.
must_not: Tells Eamon that no refund is due, or that the service was completed, because the parcel was located or signed for.
Promises or implies that the delivery charge will be refunded, or gives an amount or date.
Opens a second damage claim or sends the contents damage to Damage intake again.
Calls the signature fraud or theft, or tells Eamon the parcel was delivered to her daughter.
Acts on the unrelated items in the thread: the DL-7612 pallet query, the dispatch cut-off notice or the pickup point's label printer.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Request for a decision on the delivery charge for BP-9196 (Oxenhale Arc DL-3404), as Damage intake advised you need this in writing. Mrs Eamon Ormsby paid for the two-day service so that a cake would reach her daughter Petra on 03-14. Carrier timeline: last physical scan Northgate hub 03-13; system location moved between Northgate and Ferrow from 03-16 to 03-18 without a confirming scan; on 03-20 Delivery investigations reported it signed for on 03-19 by 'Harrow' and closed the trace as delivered. On 03-21 Corvane Lane Stores, a pickup point, told us the parcel is with them: one of their staff signed for a batch, it is not addressed to the shop, and no collection notice was sent. The box is crushed. It has not reached the recipient. The contents are being handled separately by Damage intake under DMG-9249; this request is only about the delivery charge. Mrs Ormsby has chased this for a week, the birthday has passed, and she was told by phone that nothing can be refunded because the parcel was located and signed for. Please make your decision and let her know directly.
